title: A-13: close the stale Windows-launcher clutter finding with a measurement gate
businessRules: A-13 (MEDIUM, PARTIAL) is canonical in config/product-completeness.json. It closes only when a dependency-free test proves the Ubuntu workflow carries zero Windows-first launchers; editing the status string alone is forbidden.

The finding has been PARTIAL since the 957-file audit, but the launchers it describes were removed in an earlier wave and nobody re-measured and closed it. That is the A-14 class of defect - a status that lags the evidence - and must not be closed by assertion.

Measured 2026-10-14 before intake: zero tracked .bat, .cmd, .ps1 or .vbs files anywhere in git ls-files; zero of the 123 package.json scripts invoke cmd.exe, powershell, notepad or a .bat/.cmd target; the only docs/ line matching a Windows command is the A-13 acceptance criterion itself, which states the goal rather than instructing a Windows path.

The Windows code that remains in scripts/*.mjs is correctly platform-guarded cross-platform developer support, gated on process.platform === win32 or an isWindows constant, and is a no-op on Ubuntu. It is not operator clutter and must not be deleted; the rule forbids Windows-first operator paths, not the existence of win32 branches.

The Ubuntu operator path is npm/Node/Bash, already stated in docs/TOKO360-MASTER-PRODUCT-COMPLETION-WORKFLOW.md sections 8 and the P6 launcher-removal bullet. This work item converts that prose claim into a failing gate.
No business logic, API contract, permission, tenant or branch authority, schema, runtime path or gate predicate may change, and no existing assertion may be weakened.
acceptanceCriteria: A dependency-free test fails if any tracked file matches an extension that is a Windows-first launcher (.bat, .cmd, .ps1, .vbs) or if any package.json script invokes cmd.exe, powershell, notepad, or a .bat/.cmd target.
The same test passes today, proving the measurement is real and not aspirational.
The test allows win32 branches inside Node scripts, because platform-guarded developer support is not operator clutter; the assertion is about operator-facing launchers and npm entry points only.
docs/TOKO360-MASTER-PRODUCT-COMPLETION-WORKFLOW.md keeps its Ubuntu-first statements; no Windows-first operator instruction is reintroduced.
audit:A-13 moves from PARTIAL to RUNTIME_VERIFIED with resolvable evidence, and the open-finding count drops from 3 to 2.
Both GitHub heavy workflows and Workflow Governance stay green on the exact commit.
testPlan: node --test tests/ubuntu-workflow-windows-launchers.test.mjs - new control; a synthetic .cmd file and a synthetic windows-only npm script must each fail it
npm run lint, npm run workflow:validate, npm run validate:repo, npm run audit:full:repo
GitHub exact-source Full Automated UAT and Full System Simulation - green with productionTouched false
migrationPlan: No schema migration. Only one dependency-free test changes; no database object is added, altered or dropped.
rollbackPlan: Revert the commit. The launcher gate disappears and A-13 returns to PARTIAL; nothing else changes, no data is written and no runtime path is affected. The prior green commit remains a valid checkpoint.
monitoringPlan: The test runs inside test:dependency-free on every local run and on both heavy workflows, so a reintroduced Windows launcher fails the build rather than quietly re-cluttering the Ubuntu path.
securityNotes: No secret, token, database URL, credential or personal data appears in this work item or in any file it edits, and none may be introduced. The platform-guarded win32 branches that remain are developer convenience only and are unreachable on Ubuntu.
